summary: A planned campus of up to four leading-edge DRAM fabs in the Town of Clay, Onondaga County, New York, to be built over two decades or more. Micron held the official groundbreaking for the first fab in January 2026 and poured the first foundation concrete in July 2026, ahead of its plan. The company expects initial wafer output from the first fab in calendar 2030, with later fabs ramping through the decade.

metrics.note: Covers the full campus of up to four fabs.
CHIPS Act direct funding agreements signed in December 2024 for one Boise fab and two Clay, New York fabs; amended in June 2025 to add the second Boise fab without raising the total.
Non-binding term sheet with New York State for tax credits and job wage incentives over 20-plus years, as described in Micron's FY2026 annual report.
Combined cleanroom for all four planned fabs, from the undated federal award page.
Direct Micron jobs; state and company figures of up to 50,000 include supply-chain and community jobs.

milestones.note: First foundation concrete poured, marking the move from site preparation to vertical construction.
Initial wafer output expected in calendar 2030.

notes: Micron has not named the individual Clay fabs, so the campus is one project record and dates for the first fab carry the phase label Fab 1. Federal CHIPS funding covers the first two Clay fabs. The state's July 2026 release also reports foundation work starting less than six months after groundbreaking.
